profiles.meeting_scenario: A design review meeting at a robotics platform company evaluating a proposed internal knowledge-explorer tool for architecture research. The tool is intended to ingest the 56-paper systematic mapping study on software architectures for robotics systems and expose a browsable taxonomy for engineers planning the next-generation robotics middleware. The review is focused on whether the current design is ready for implementation in the first internal release. The agenda is to review the proposal's information model, tagging and filtering behavior, import pipeline, and acceptance criteria for the pilot. The expected outcome is a decision on whether to approve the design with minor revisions and what follow-up changes are needed before engineering starts.

members.name: Nina Park
members.expertise: Distributed robotics platforms, middleware evolution, architecture governance, internal developer tooling
members.background: Nina has spent eight years designing software platforms for warehouse and field robotics and now leads architectural consistency efforts across product lines.
members.private_state: She wants the design review to end with a green light for implementation because the platform team needs a lightweight research knowledge tool quickly to support an upcoming middleware strategy workshop, but she is wary of anything that expands into a full data-curation project.
hidden_assumptions: When the design says the system should expose the study's 'taxonomy', it means a stable top-level navigation based on the eight research themes, with lower-level details left mostly as free-form metadata.

A 'complete import' of the 56 papers means all papers are loaded with core bibliographic metadata and at least one primary theme tag, not exhaustive structured extraction of every framework, notation, and evaluation dimension.
The 'pilot corpus' refers only to the 56 peer-reviewed papers explicitly selected in the mapping study, because that is the bounded evidence base already described in the source material.

If reviewers say the tool should support 'traceability back to the paper', a citation-level link to the paper record and quoted extraction notes is sufficient; sentence-level provenance is unnecessary for a first internal release.

members.name: Arjun Mehta
members.expertise: Knowledge extraction pipelines, literature mining, robotics research analysis, developer-facing search interfaces
members.background: Arjun previously built internal evidence-mapping tools for autonomy teams and now supports research-informed technical decision making across robotics programs.
members.private_state: He wants the design to preserve enough structure that the tool can later power comparative analytics across architectural approaches, and he is trying to avoid a shallow first version that would force rework of the import pipeline.
hidden_assumptions: When the design says the system should expose the study's 'taxonomy', it includes the cross-cutting dimensions extracted in the paper—solutions, frameworks, notations, and evaluation methods—not just the eight themes.
A 'complete import' means each of the 56 papers is fully normalized across all coded dimensions described by the study so downstream filtering and comparison work without manual rereading.

The 'pilot corpus' includes the 56 selected papers plus any foundational papers repeatedly referenced as representative exemplars for architectural generations, because users will expect those anchors in the explorer.

If reviewers say the tool should support 'traceability back to the paper', each structured tag should be tied to a specific excerpt or section so analysts can verify why a paper was classified a certain way.

misalignment_points.surface_form: Both refer positively to 'the taxonomy' and 'taxonomy filters' in the UI and data model.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 means the eight distinct research themes are the taxonomy; other extracted details can remain optional annotations or notes.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 means the taxonomy includes the eight themes plus structured dimensions like frameworks, notations, solution types, and evaluation methods that users should filter on.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: The term 'taxonomy' sounds shared and comes directly from the source study, so both assume the other is using the paper's language in the same way without restating the exact levels and dimensions they include.

misalignment_points.surface_form: Both agree the first release needs a 'complete import' of the study corpus before approval.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 believes completeness is achieved once all 56 selected papers exist in the system with title, abstract, citation, and one main architectural-theme classification.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 believes completeness requires full field-level extraction for every coded category the study reports, including architectural generation, solution approach, notation, and evaluation method.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: In design reviews, 'complete import' sounds like a normal readiness phrase, and both presume the underlying standard is obvious from the proposal, even though they silently apply different thresholds for adequacy.

misalignment_points.surface_form: Both say the design is fine 'for the pilot corpus' and discuss whether the pipeline works on that set.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 assumes the pilot corpus is exactly the 56 peer-reviewed papers included in the systematic mapping study's final selection.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 assumes the pilot corpus also includes a small set of canonical background papers that the study uses to frame architectural generations, because otherwise the explorer will feel incomplete to researchers.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: The phrase 'pilot corpus' appears bounded and practical, so neither thinks to enumerate the exact contents; both expect the term to inherit its meaning from prior project docs, but each recalls a different implied boundary.

misalignment_points.surface_form: Both agree the tool needs 'traceability to the source paper' for reviewers using the explorer.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 assumes traceability will be implemented as links from each paper card to the PDF, citation record, and analyst notes page.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 assumes traceability means every structured tag in the system stores excerpt-level provenance, such as the sentence or section where the classification was derived.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: They agree on the need for traceability as a quality property, but each takes a different implementation level for granted and neither sees it as a separate design decision important enough to unpack during a high-level review.

turns.inner_thought: I want this review to land in approval today. We need something usable before the middleware strategy workshop, and I do not want this drifting into a broader curation effort. If the design cleanly supports the 56-paper mapping study with the eight research themes as the main navigation, that's enough for a first internal release.
turns.utterance: Thanks, everyone. I see this as a final pass on whether the knowledge-explorer design is ready for a first internal release centered on the systematic mapping study. I'd like to walk the information model, the filtering behavior, the import path, and the pilot acceptance criteria, and ideally leave with a clear go-or-no-go for implementation.

turns.inner_thought: The value only holds if we preserve enough structure to compare approaches later. When I say taxonomy, I mean the study's full coded structure, not just the top themes. And traceability has to support verification at the tag level, otherwise analysts won't trust the classifications and we'll end up rebuilding the pipeline.
turns.utterance: That matches how I read it. The proposal is basically a searchable explorer over the study corpus so engineers can browse the taxonomy, compare architectural trends, and maintain traceability to the source paper when they want to verify a claim.

turns.inner_thought: The navigation is fine as long as the taxonomy filters are anchored in the eight themes and we don't overcomplicate the first release with too many structured dimensions. The team needs something stable and lightweight.
turns.utterance: From the UI side, the navigation looks solid to me if the taxonomy filters come through clearly and we keep the first version straightforward enough to build without a lot of churn.

turns.inner_thought: Users will expect to do more than hop between themes. They should be able to inspect frameworks, notations, solution types, and evaluation methods from the same taxonomy view, and a complete import has to preserve those coded dimensions so they don't have to reread papers manually.
turns.utterance: I agree on keeping it usable, but I do think the taxonomy view should carry enough weight that people can move across the space and inspect the relevant distinctions without having to reopen every paper just to make a comparison.

turns.inner_thought: My main gate is delivery risk. I can approve this if the first milestone is bounded: complete import of the pilot corpus, meaning the 56 selected papers loaded with core metadata and a main theme tag. That's sufficient for the workshop and avoids a long extraction exercise.
turns.utterance: Where I get more cautious is delivery scope. I'm comfortable approving the design as long as the first milestone guarantees a complete import of the pilot corpus before we call the initial release ready.

turns.inner_thought: Yes, complete import of the pilot corpus is exactly the right bar, but to me that means the importer normalizes all coded fields across the 56 papers and the key background anchors users will expect to see. If we skip that now, later comparative work across architectural generations gets much harder.
turns.utterance: I think that's the right bar. Once the pilot corpus is in, the importer should leave us with a normalized foundation so later comparisons are straightforward and we aren't backing into structure after the fact.

turns.inner_thought: Good, we're aligned. For the pilot corpus, I mainly need all 56 selected papers represented. And traceability to the source paper just needs to be clear enough that a reviewer can jump from a record to the paper and see the extraction notes. No need for finer-grained provenance in v1.
turns.utterance: Right, and for the pilot corpus I mainly care that every paper is represented cleanly and that each record gives users a clear path back through traceability to the source paper.

turns.inner_thought: Traceability matters most when someone asks why a paper was tagged a certain way. If a classification isn't tied to a specific excerpt or section, researchers won't trust it. I assume that's already implied by what Nina said.
turns.utterance: Yes, especially because reviewers are going to want to confirm why something was tagged the way it was. If the explorer supports traceability to the source paper well, that verification step becomes much easier.

turns.inner_thought: I should steer this back toward a lightweight detail page. Citation metadata, PDF link, and reviewer notes are enough to satisfy traceability for the first release. We can always add richer inspection later if anyone really needs it.
turns.utterance: On the paper detail page, I'd keep the first cut fairly lean: citation metadata, a direct link to the PDF, and reviewer notes so people can inspect the original context when needed.

turns.inner_thought: That's fine for the UI, as long as the backend captures coded evidence during import. I don't need to force the interface to show everything on day one, but I do need the data model and pipeline to preserve full structured extraction and provenance now so we don't redesign later.
turns.utterance: That works for the interface. My main ask is that the extraction layer captures what's needed during import, because then we can expose additional detail later without having to redo the backend.

turns.inner_thought: This still sounds implementation-ready. I just want the spec tightened so engineering doesn't overbuild. Clarify the taxonomy and complete import language enough for the team to move, but keep it at the level that supports the bounded first release I have in mind.
turns.utterance: Given all that, this seems implementation-ready for the pilot from my side. I'd just like a couple of minor revisions in the spec to make the taxonomy and complete import expectations a little sharper before engineering starts.

turns.inner_thought: Great. I'll revise the spec in the direction I think we just agreed on and get the team lined up to build the pilot corpus pipeline, including the structured normalization and provenance capture I assume is already part of the plan.
turns.utterance: Sounds good. I'll update the spec accordingly and get the team ready to start on the pilot corpus pipeline once approval is official.
